Non-ruminant digestive system

Digestion process of ruminants:

1. Prehension and mastication
  o Prehension is the act of gathering food using the tongue and lips and moves it into the mouth.
  o Mastication is the chewing and grinding of the food into smaller particles.

Prehension
Mastication

2. Swallowing
  o Ruminants swallow feed rapidly without chewing food adequately.
  o Tongue helps guide the feed to the esophagus.
  o Saliva of ruminants does not have enzymes unlike monogastrics.

facts: The non-ruminant digestive system diagram depicts the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, cecum, large intestine, and anus in a monogastric animal (pig).
Prehension is the act of gathering food using the tongue and lips and moving it into the mouth.
Mastication is the chewing and grinding of food into smaller particles.
During initial feeding, ruminants swallow feed rapidly without chewing food adequately.
The tongue helps guide feed into the esophagus during swallowing.
The saliva of ruminants does not contain enzymes, unlike that of monogastrics.
